title: My Brother's Husband
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Yaichi, a single father in suburban Tokyo, is visited by Mike Flanagan, the Canadian widower of his estranged, recently deceased twin brother Ryoji. Over Mike's three-week stay, Yaichi's daughter Kana embraces Mike at once, while Yaichi slowly confronts the quiet discomfort with his brother's homosexuality that drove them apart, and the neighborhood, school and old friends react. The family parts with Mike as kin.
life_message: Family is made by love and acceptance, and quiet everyday prejudice wounds both its targets and those who hold it.

content.note: Same-sex marriage discussed; a clean bath scene showing male bodies (NPR, which calls it all-ages); no sex.
Mourning, estrangement and a closeted friend's isolation (Wikipedia; MangaUpdates Mourning).

dominant: Acceptance of gay family members; critique of quiet homophobia; family as chosen bond

delivery.note: The traditional view is explored mainly inside Yaichi, who is treated with sympathy as he changes; outside objectors appear briefly.

winners_losers: Yaichi, Kana and Mike become family; quiet prejudice is what loses; sympathy goes to Mike, Ryoji and the closeted characters.
